title: American Express Company FY2022 Form 10-K — Business Environment (T&E momentum vs G&S deceleration; inflation contribution)
key_points: T&E spending momentum remained strong throughout 2022.
Year-over-year Goods & Services spending growth slowed toward the end of 2022 after large pandemic-recovery growth rates earlier in the year.
Management describes inflation as a modest contributor to billed business growth.
Strengthening of the U.S. dollar had a negative impact on international billings.
raw_excerpt: T&E spending momentum remained strong throughout the year, while year-over-year Goods & Services spending growth slowed towards the end of the year following the large pandemic recovery growth rates experienced earlier in the year. Inflation was a modest contributor to our strong billed business growth, while the continuing strengthening of the U.S. dollar, relative to the prior year, against most major currencies in which we operate, had a negative impact on our international billings.

title: American Express Company 2022 Form 10-K — Business Environment (MD&A)
key_points: Net card fees increased 17 percent year-over-year in 2022, attributed to new card acquisitions reaching record levels and Card Member retention remaining high.
The company attributes high retention to investments in its premium value propositions.
Worldwide network volumes increased 21 percent year-over-year (24 percent FX-adjusted); billed business increased 23 percent (25 percent FX-adjusted).
U.S. Consumer billed business grew 24 percent year-over-year; Commercial Services billed business grew 21 percent; International billed business grew 23 percent (36 percent FX-adjusted).
Total revenues net of interest expense increased 25 percent year-over-year (27 percent FX-adjusted).
Net interest income increased 28 percent versus prior year, primarily driven by growth in Card Member loans.
The rising interest rate environment had a fairly neutral impact on full-year results, but rising rates had a modest negative impact on net interest income toward the end of the year.
Card Member loans increased 22 percent year-over-year, with the majority of growth coming from existing Card Members.
Provisions for credit losses reflected a reserve build of $617 million in 2022 versus a reserve release of $2.5 billion in 2021.
Credit metrics remain below pre-pandemic levels.
Net income was $7.5 billion ($9.85 per share) in 2022 versus $8.1 billion ($10.02 per share) in 2021.
The company states its investments led to increased generational relevance with Millennial and Gen Z customers, record new card acquisitions, and deeper customer relationships.

title: American Express 2022 Form 10-K — Risk Factors: inflation and cost pressure on the premium value proposition
key_points: The company states that increased costs as a result of inflation, colleague retention and recruitment, supply chain issues and shortages of materials such as chips for cards may require it to reduce investments in other areas.

The company states that if marketing, promotion, rewards and Card Member services expenses increase beyond expectations, it would need to offset the impact by increasing fee-based revenues, decreasing operating expenses, or both.
The company notes that many credit card issuers have instituted rewards and cobrand programs that may be similar to or more attractive than its own.
The company identifies Amazon and Delta as its two largest Membership Rewards redemption partners.

title: American Express 2022 Form 10-K — Competition section and cobrand concentration
key_points: The company states it competes in the global payments industry with card networks, issuers and acquirers, paper-based transactions, bank transfer models, and alternative payment mechanisms.
The company states it believes Visa and Mastercard are larger than it is in most countries.
All cobrand portfolios in aggregate accounted for approximately 18 percent of worldwide network volumes for the year ended December 31, 2022.
Card Member loans related to cobrand portfolios accounted for approximately 36 percent of worldwide Card Member loans as of December 31, 2022.
The company states that cobrand partnerships are highly competitive among card issuers and networks because they typically appeal to high-spending loyal customers.
No named peer issuer (JPMorgan Chase, Capital One, Discover, Citigroup) is quantitatively compared anywhere in the filing.

title: American Express 2022 Form 10-K — Macroeconomic scenario assumptions used for credit reserves
key_points: Reserve calculations used a U.S. unemployment rate scenario range of 4 percent for Q4 2022, 3-6 percent for Q1 2023, 3-8 percent for Q4 2023, and 3-7 percent for Q4 2024.
Reserve calculations used U.S. GDP growth (contraction) scenarios of (0.1) percent for Q4 2022, 5 to (1) percent for Q1 2023, 6 to 0.2 percent for Q4 2023, and 3 to 2 percent for Q4 2024.

The Card Member loans reserve for credit losses increased in 2022 primarily driven by an increase in loans outstanding, higher delinquencies and changes in macroeconomic forecasts, partially offset by release of COVID-19 pandemic-driven reserves.

The Card Member loans reserve for credit losses decreased in 2021 primarily due to improved portfolio quality and macroeconomic forecasts, largely driven by improvement in unemployment rate projections.
